title: Existence of I-sections
statement_scope: Whole Proposition 2.5.3: let pi: L_S -> S be a map of topological spaces and mu: R x L_S -> L_S a continuous R-action preserving each fiber of pi and satisfying axioms (A1), (A2), (A4) and (A5) of Theorem 2.4.1. Then for every point s in S there exists an open set U subset S containing s, a finite linearly ordered set I, and an I-section of the projection map L_S x_S U -> U.

difficulty_reason: author-work-bearing-core-v1-20261114: H2 because Proposition 2.5.3 at author PDF p.17 constructs local I-sections for a family satisfying (A1),(A2),(A4),(A5), choosing the finite fixed point list x_0<...<x_n, lifting across non-fixed components by (A5), separating fixed loci by (A2), ordering them by (A4), and invoking continuity of d_{L_S} from Proposition 2.4.4; the argument is a non-routine local construction needed for Theorem 2.4.1.

difficulty_evidence.bearing_core: Builds local I-sections by combining the local lifting property, unramified fixed locus, order-closedness and continuity of translation distance, ensuring each non-fixed component is met.
